capabilities: Sync a vault two-way to Google Drive or Cloud Storage
Encrypt note content end-to-end before upload
Propagate deletions and keep both copies on conflict
Authenticate with a user-created Google OAuth client or an HMAC key
Sync from Obsidian desktop and mobile
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Users must create their own Google OAuth client; versions 0.6.x and earlier used a bundled shared client that was removed, so upgrading requires signing in again. Details are deferred to a SECURITY.md in the repository, and a 0.6.x-to-newer migration caveat plus OAuth token-expiry caveats are documented.
motivation: The author believes keeping notes backed up and in sync shouldn't require a subscription, routing the vault through someone else's server, or letting a plugin rewrite files.
problem: Obsidian's built-in sync options route data through a third-party service or cost a subscription, and users who want their vault on their own Google storage have no first-party option.

relations.evidence: Google Drive — sync to your personal Drive with your ordinary Google account.
Google Cloud Storage — for those already on Google Cloud. Sync to your own bucket.

requires.name: Google account with a user-created OAuth client (or a Cloud Storage HMAC key)

summary: Two-way vault sync to your own Google Drive or Google Cloud Storage bucket, with optional end-to-end encryption and no third-party server.
